milestone: Reader cursor URL boundary / A-02 / A-06
scenario: Opaque pagination cursors remain recoverable in URL state; oversized incoming trails reset to the first page and an unrepresentable next page cannot advance the UI.

measurement_before_repair.command: node --import tsx --input-type=module -e 'measure buildWorkbenchHref for normal, max, and oversized trails'

failure_before_repair.result: failed: oversized trail was accepted and appendCursorForNextPage returned a 25-item stack

failure_before_repair.command: npx playwright test e2e/service-worker.smoke.spec.ts --project=chromium -g "oversized cursor trails"
failure_before_repair.result: failed by timeout when the local fixture HTTP entry was asked to navigate a 94KB URL; this was recorded as a transport-size limitation, not a product pass

repair: Added an 8192-character workbench href budget and a 7680-character encoded cursor-trail budget, with raw-trail parsing bounded before JSON.parse.
Normalized oversized incoming trails to the first page and redirected malformed/non-canonical reader workbench URLs while preserving module, sort, language, query, and return article context.
Prevented next-page state from advancing when the new cursor cannot be serialized; the user receives a recoverable error toast instead of a page-two result under a page-one URL.
Added final pushState validation so a pagination transition cannot silently omit its trail.

validation.command: npx playwright test e2e/service-worker.smoke.spec.ts --project=chromium -g "oversized cursor trails"
validation.result: pass: 1 test using a transportable approximately 7.8KB oversized trail

validation.command: npx playwright test e2e/service-worker.smoke.spec.ts --project=chromium -g "later-page article return|scan mode paging failure|scan mode error offers a previous-page escape"

validation.result: pass: Next.js production build and TypeScript validation

known_limit: The 94KB URL cannot be used as a browser proof through the local fixture HTTP entry because navigation timed out; the behavioral proof uses a transportable 7.8KB over-budget trail. No production proxy, real API, staging/production service, database, or provider was accessed.
